recentItems.title: How Harambe kickstarted Gen Z culture | Alex Garfin | TEDxBerlin
recentItems.description:
He convinced us to let him do a TEDx Talk about Harambe. Though he really ended up giving us all insight into Gen-Z Culture. Alex Garfin, born September 23rd 2003, is an internationally acclaimed actor and youth activist who has dedicated his personal life to uniting people. His acting career spans over a decade with highlights including playing “Superboy” in “Superman and Lois,” “Linus” in “The Peanuts Movie” and a storied on-stage career in NYC. 

In his advocacy career, he serves as the head of youth and board secretary of the UN ECOSOC NGO World Information Transfer leading a staff of ten young people at UNHQ. He is the founder of The Alethos Initiative, a nonprofit that gives influencers journalism training and access to experts to fight the spread of misinformation online. He says the roots of his advocacy work are in his travels engaging with people on a grassroots level around the world. He has been to 24 countries so far, including the Middle East, the far east, Africa and 30 American states. He plans to continue to engage in grassroots dialogue domestically and abroad. 

This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

recentItems.title: The Future of Living | Zack Kass | TEDxMiami
recentItems.description:
Zack Kass's talk challenges us to rethink the narrative around technological progress, innovation, and impact- through the lens of historical events. 

His talk explores how we can become an active participant in the future that delivers more agency, dignity, and time. Zack Kass has spent more than sixteen years at the forefront of artificial intelligence.

As Head of Go-to-Market at OpenAI, he led the teams responsible for sales, partnerships, and customer success, turning the company’s cutting-edge research into real-world business solutions, and growing revenue from millions to billions. 

Since then he has advised more than 500 of the Global 5000, taught at University of Virginia and Hong Kong University of Science and Technology, and published his first book, an international bestseller, The Next RenAIssance: AI and the Expansion of Human Potential.

His mission is to ensure everyone can be an active participant in future that delivers more agency, dignity, and time. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

recentItems.title: Is AI changing how we learn? | Dr. Marcus Fontoura | TEDxMiami
recentItems.description:
As artificial intelligence evolves, it’s changing how we learn.

Marcus Fontoura walks us through a transformative journey of learning and what it means for us and generations to come. His talk explores what parts of learning will remain fundamentally unchanged and what will likely change with AI. 
 Marcus Fontoura is currently in his second tenure as Technical Fellow and Corporate Vice President at Microsoft, where he works as CTO for Azure Core. He is also the author of A Platform Mindset: My lessons from developer to CTO, published in 2025 by 8080 Books.

Most recently, he was the CTO at Stone.co (2022 2025), where he led the engineering organization. Previously, in his first tenure as Technical Fellow and Corporate Vice President at Microsoft (2013-2022), Marcus worked as the chief architect for Azure Compute and led the Azure efficiency team. Marcus also had posts at Google, Yahoo, and IBM Research. He was a post-doctoral researcher at Princeton University and has received his Ph.D. in Computer Science by the Pontifical Catholic University of Rio de Janeiro, in Brazil (PUC-Rio) This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

recentItems.title: AI ethics and the future of safety | Dr. Roman Yampolskiy | TEDxMiami
recentItems.description:
As artificial intelligence grows more powerful, so do the risks. In this riveting talk, Dr. Roman Yampolskiy looks at the long-term implications of advanced artificial intelligence. 

His talk asks one of the most important questions of our time: Can we control what we create?
 Roman V. Yampolskiy is a tenured associate professor in the department of Computer Science and Engineering at the Speed School of Engineering, University of Louisville (2008-). He is the founding and current director of the Cyber Security Lab and an author of many books including Artificial Superintelligence: a Futuristic Approach. During his tenure at UofL, Dr. Yampolskiy has been recognized as: Distinguished Teaching Professor, Professor of the Year, Faculty Favorite, Top 4 Faculty, Leader in Engineering Education, Top 10 of Online College Professor of the Year, and Outstanding Early Career in Education award winner among many other honors and distinctions. Yampolskiy is a Senior member of IEEE, AGI and Member of Kentucky Academy of Science. Dr. Yampolskiy’s main areas of interest are AI Safety and Cybersecurity. Dr. Yampolskiy is an author of over 300 publications including multiple journal articles and books. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

recentItems.title: The Future of  Human Meaning | Camille Carlton | TEDxMiami
recentItems.description:
At a time when our lives are increasingly shaped by algorithms, Camille Carlton's insightful talk explores a critical question: Who is technology really serving?

Camille makes the case for technology designed in the public interest- not just for growth, but also for impact.

 Camille is Senior Director of Strategy and Impact at the Center for Humane Technology, where she works to ensure AI is guided by the public interest. Recognized as one of Business Insider's AI 100, she shapes national debates through litigation, legislative engagement, and public narrative strategies that translate complex technology issues into public action. With a background spanning public policy, industry, and academic research, she brings a cross-disciplinary lens to the most urgent technology questions of our time. Her work has been featured in The New York Times, Bloomberg, NBC News, MIT, and more. She holds a master's from the London School of Economics, where she studied technology and development. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

recentItems.title: 戏剧不是生活的解药，但它能给你一把接住情绪的椅子 | 易阳 赵 | TEDxNanshan Salon
recentItems.description:
“戏剧是什么？”这是戏剧导演赵易阳反复思考、并尝试回答的问题。
在他看来， 戏剧不仅是一种表演艺术，更像是一把隐形的椅子，让那些无处安放的情绪坐下来，得以被看见。
在这场演讲中，他以简单而真实的故事切入，从木河马的孤独到小山村的戏剧社，他让我们看到：在戏剧的世界里，没有对错，只有“尝试”；这是一种开放的拥抱，能帮助每个人看见自己，看见彼此。
戏剧就像一座桥梁，在生活的洪流中，连接孤独与共鸣，安全地接住隐藏的情绪与故事，并将之缓缓导向治愈与希望。 深圳超级猴戏剧Club创始人
戏剧导演 This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx
